description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Support integrated management of the Luki/Mayombe, Mai-NdombÃ© and South Ubangi tropical forest Landscapes to facilitate conservation of natural resources, local development, food security and climate change mitigation and adaptation in DRC, with an innovative approach to strengthening cross-border collaboration in land use planning , as well as transboundary management of watersheds (Ubangi River) between the Central African Republic (CAR) and the DRC in South Ubangi.

The project is justified by its holistic approach to the root causes of deforestation and degradation. Unlike other initiatives that may focus solely on conservation or development, this project integrates both approches, to ensure that conservation efforts are sustainable and beneficial to local communities. This holistic approach is essential to achieving long-term environmental and socio-economic benefits.Ccomponent 1 aims to establish cross-sectoral platforms for policy coordination, conducting biodiversity assessments to integrate conservation into land use plans and cross-boundary dialogue for harmonised management of cross-border ecosystems and endangered species. The overall goal is to balance environmental conservation with socio-economic development, fostering resilience and prosperity in the region. The project will facilitate advances in adopting, integrating and harmonising policies and regulatory frameworks positive to forest conservation and indigenous peoples’ rights.Under Component 3, the project will update the assessment of local priority areas for forest restoration using the Restoration Opportunity Assessment Methodology (ROAM). Stakeholders will use ROAM and/or ICF methodology to assess and prioritise areas with the greatest potential for restoration in the three landscapes. In carrying out this assessment, stakeholders will identify key restoration opportunities based on ecological, social and economic criteria, considering factors such as biodiversity value, connectivity and stakeholder engagement. This assessment will guide the decision-making and planning processes for restoration efforts, ensuring that resources are allocated efficiently to maximise the ecological and socio-economic benefits of restoration activities.Overall, the training and materials developed under this project will strengthen the capacity of local authorities to provide advice on sustainable land-use planning and forest conservation using extension and communication materials. The project will ensure that these services are integrated into local authority processes and budgets, to maintain support for landscape restoration efforts after GEF funding ends. This collaboration between IUCN, IFAD and the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (MEDD) aims to create a resilient framework for continued environmental and socio-economic benefits.
